items.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
items.summary: The article demonstrates that generalist AI models outperform specialist policies in robot manipulation tasks, offering more reliable control via agentic manipulation policies.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should note this could streamline robotic deployment and reduce reliance on task-specific training.

items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.summary: The paper proposes CPU-ARC, a method that caches reasoning steps so a language model can reuse solutions for new problems, reducing redundant computation.
items.whyItMatters: It cuts inference costs and speeds up LLM-powered applications by reusing prior reasoning.

items.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
items.summary: The paper shows that one‑hidden‑layer ReLU networks with up to N neurons form a weakly closed set in Sobolev space, ensuring existence of minimizers for certain energies.
items.whyItMatters: It guarantees convergence and optimality for training methods like Deep Ritz and Lipschitz learning in practical neural network design.

items.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
items.summary: FlowMoP introduces a stochastic multi-person motion prediction model using conditional flow matching to generate diverse future trajectories.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more realistic, uncertainty-aware planning for autonomous systems interacting with crowds.

items.title: Graded convolutional networks: scale invariance without the scale and robustness to unknown blur
items.summary: The paper shows how graded convolutional networks achieve scale invariance and blur robustness by using scale-normalized jets and weighted sphere retractions.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it offers a principled way to build CNNs that handle scale changes and unknown blur.

items.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The paper examines how reliable majority‑vote pseudo‑labels are for test‑time reinforcement learning of language models, dissecting bias and rollout noise.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding label reliability can improve domain adaptation and reduce costly manual labeling for AI developers.

items.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
items.summary: CodeQuant2 introduces outlier mitigation and adaptive clustering to improve low‑precision quantization of large reasoning models during early decoding steps.
items.whyItMatters: It reduces inference costs while preserving reasoning accuracy, benefiting developers deploying LLMs on resource‑constrained hardware.

items.title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
items.summary: The paper introduces GRAC, a graph-based retrieval-augmented model that generates surgical scene captions to streamline operative report creation.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it automates documentation, saving time and improving surgical training.

items.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: The paper presents Grasp-TAGS, a method for selecting task-aware grasps using critic distillation to improve mobile manipulators’ long-horizon loco‑manipulation.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a way to boost reliability in service and warehouse robots that must move and manipulate large objects.

items.title: Flow-Guided Target-Space Alignment via Path Consistency
items.summary: The paper proposes a flow-guided method that aligns source data into a target modality’s space, preserving global structure and instance-level pairing for downstream use.
items.whyItMatters: It improves multimodal integration, enabling more accurate cross-modal analysis and better downstream performance.

items.title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
items.summary: The study tests if a sender using only hashes, with a language model at the receiver, can send short English texts more cheaply than a fully trained sender.
items.whyItMatters: It explores cost‑efficient text transmission for edge devices and low‑bandwidth scenarios.

items.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
items.summary: The article argues embodied AI can shift to general-purpose models by treating physical interactions as digital software tasks, enabling versatile agents.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers should watch this for its potential to unify robotics and software AI, simplifying development and deployment.

items.title: Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
items.summary: This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. The core intuition is that inter-model agreement on semantics is informative about truth, and that an LLM-as-judge can provide higher-fidelity pairwise assessments than traditional string- or embedding-based metrics. We operationalise this…

items.title: Fifty-Two Shades of Pig: What the UCR Archive Really Asks Classifiers to Do
items.summary: The pigs were bleeding. That was the point of the experiment: could airway pressure reveal hemorrhage before it became critical? In the UCR Time Series Classification Archive, the de facto benchmark for Time Series Classification (TSC), the same recordings ask a different question: "which of 52 pigs produced this trace?". items.title: Can Agentic Systems Close the Gap in Radiology with Production AI Tools?
items.summary: Radiology AI has developed along two paths: specialized models that perform well on narrow tasks but cover few clinical findings, and generalist models that address a broader range of tasks but remain prone to hallucination and inaccurate measurements. Combining the two through agentic systems offers a route towards comprehensive radiology reporting, but published systems are tied to one modality…

items.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) rewards are notoriously difficult to design and control, often leading to the model learning unintended behaviors such as reward hacking. One potential solution is to monitor for reward hacking and penalize it when detected; however, training against a monitor could lead to evasive behavior, and our general understanding of how to apply monitors effectively during…

items.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
items.summary: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented…

items.title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
items.summary: The timeline by which quantum computers can solve breakthrough problems in science depends on improved quantum algorithms as much as on better hardware. Such algorithmic advances are typically achieved through many years of expert human collaboration. In mathematics and computer science, large language models have accelerated progress through automated discovery loops. However, quantum algorithms…

items.title: Generative Latent Priors for Interpreting and Steering Protein Language Models
items.summary: Dominant methods for interpreting large models impose strong structural assumptions. Generative Latent Priors (GLP) are a complementary approach: a diffusion model that learns the distribution of a frozen model's activations directly, imposing no assumptions. We port GLP to ESM-2 activations (UniRef50) and evaluate it at two host scales (ESM-2-8M and -650M), both as a lens for protein…

items.title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
items.summary: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years. This chapter gives an introduction and summary to the use of ML methods to optimize lattice field theory without introducing any uncontrolled approximations. We focus on those directions which are clearly established as of late 2025, marking the…
